sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tailoring of Licensed Theatrical Costume Robes and Synthetic Wigs

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – federal constitutional and common-law framework; Quebec is a civil-law jurisdiction for private and commercial matters (Civil Code of Quebec); commercial registration governed by the provincial Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, effective 1 April 2021
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada since 30 December 2018

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and FINTRAC regulations (SOR/2002-184 and SOR/2007-121); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (Part II.1); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Canada Business Corporations Act beneficial-ownership amendments (C-42, in force 22 January 2024); Quebec: An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Limited Partnership Act, SQ 2023, c 2; Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991 (arts 2236–2260 on partnerships).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of status / good standing of the foreign corporate general partner (or equivalent foreign partnership registration extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is a party to the Apostille Convention as of 14 January 2024); consular legalization only if the source jurisdiction is not an Apostille state; certified French translation by an OTTIAQ-accredited translator for filing at REQ

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the deed of partnership / limited partnership agreement (including name, objects, capital and allocation provisions)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin, or original executing partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then Hague Apostille of the certification, then OTTIAQ-certified French translation; translation certificate chained to the notarial copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney granting authority to the Quebec-based founding representative / designated general partner for service and registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if applicable) and certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy and proof of residential address of every general partner and every ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing public authority (police / immigration) or notarized copy by foreign notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille; certified French translation; employer or bank reference may substitute only for address verification under FINTRAC guidance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Integrity certificate / police clearance certificate for each general partner (where available), plus bankruptcy search certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police / judicial records authority of the partner's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and OTTIAQ-certified French translation; required for the REQ declaration of fitness when the general partner is a natural person

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, authorized representatives and UBOs at or above the 25% threshold against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (SEMA), the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the Criminal Code terrorist-entity list, FINTRAC public notices and, for USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe, Shopify Payments), the OFAC SDN list. PEP identification is mandatory under the PCMLTFA regulations (ss 9.1–9.3; SOR/2002-184) for domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations and their family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval are required on any PEP or sanctions hit. A written risk assessment and CDD file must be completed before registration, with records retained for five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name-reservation and registration service via the Centre d'affaires numérique (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), an enterprise name must have a French version; a non-French brand or name may be used only when accompanied by a French version or where the name is a registered trademark; Latin/French-script transliteration is mandatory, and the REQ refuses any name confusingly similar to an existing distinctive name (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, ss 15–16 and regulations).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Gouvernement du Québec / Gouvernement du Canada
LP / société en commandite (when the name is used by a non-LP entity)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects a proposed name, the Registraire issues a written refusal citing the confusing or misleading provision. The applicant may (1) immediately submit a revised name through the Centre d'affaires; (2) file the prior-name holder's written consent to coexistence; or (3) request an administrative review in writing within 30 days of the refusal (Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, s 17). If the administrative review is refused, a judicial appeal lies to the Court of Québec within 30 days of the internal decision. During the appeal the refused name may not be used; a pre-verified backup name is recommended. Name reservations may be renewed once for an additional 90 days before re-payment of the reservation tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible in Quebec only when the registered address is a real civic address within Quebec (no post-office box) and an individual or firm is designated to receive service of process. For manufacturing businesses (ISIC 3240), the REQ requires a distinct 'establishment' address for the production site; if the cosplay apparel is manufactured by a third-party workshop, that workshop address should be declared and placed on record. Pure virtual arrangements without any physical place of business will be flagged in REQ annual declarations and by financial institutions onboarding the partnership.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this sector: approximately 3%–5% annual risk of an unannounced REQ or provincial administrative visit during the first three years, based on the low-risk AML classification and the absence of a statutory operating licence. The risk rises to roughly 15% in year one if the LP is virtual-office-only with no declared production establishment, no employees and no Quebec bank account relationship.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name verification (vérification de nom) and NUANS-equivalent search against the REQ database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c P-44.1, r. 1)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Formal reservation of the proposed limited partnership name for the statutory window
Initial registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) of the société en commandite / limited partnership
Beneficial ownership (bénéficiaire ultime) declaration and partner-information filing made at registration
OTTIAQ-certified French translation of the deed of partnership, powers of attorney, certificates of status and identification documents
Hague apostille authentication of three original document sets (certificate of status, partnership deed, power of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada or the competent foreign authentication authority of the origin jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of approximately CAD 25 per document plus service/courier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of partner resolutions, power of attorney and identification declarations in the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per notarial act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office in Quebec and designated process agent (complete service-of-process capability)
UBO/KYC/PEP pre-incorporation compliance review, sanctions screening report and written CDD risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing hourly benchmark (approximately 3 hours at USD 200/hour)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Express courier, apostille scheduling and administrative contingency

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2186-2188 and 2235-2264 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ, c. P-44.1), ss. 2-7, 12-14, 24-27
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Application for Registration) filed via the Registraire des entreprises online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership. Initial capital contributions may be in cash, property or expertise, and are fixed by the private partnership agreement. No escrow account is required by law; however, a registered office in Quebec and a general partner are mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first meeting of the general partners of Cosplay Prop Apparel S.E.C., that the partnership formation statement filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is approved; that the initial capital contributions set forth in the private partnership agreement be accepted and recorded as the fixed contributions of the limited partners; that the registered office be established at [street address], Quebec, and the manager/chief administrative officer be appointed with signatory authority; that opening bank accounts and accepting funds from limited partners be authorized; and that the partnership do all further acts necessary to satisfy the legal publicity, environmental, and occupational safety requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search in REQ's central name registry. Select a legally distinct name containing the required designation 'société en commandite', 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'. If using a coined commercial name, submit the REQ online name reservation request and retain the reservation number. If no reservation is used, the partnership may carry the name of one or more general partners.
required_dossiers: REQ name search or reservation receipt
Explanation of the proposed 'Cosplay Prop Apparel' distinctive element
General partner(s) written consent to the use of the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for confusion, amend the distinctive element or file the consent of the conflicting name holder. If refusal persists, submit a new name declaration to REQ or seek a name-confirmation judgment before the Quebec Superior Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or Quebec notary in private practice; REQ is not involved at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a convention de société en commandite identifying the general partner(s), limited partner(s), name, registered office, accounting year, capital contributions, profit-sharing, management powers and dissolution terms. For immovable property ownership or bank financing, have the signatures notarized. Keep the original in the partnership records and provide certified copies to financial institutions.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement with all exhibits
Identification documents of all partners (passport, provincial ID)
Proof of registered office availability (lease, deed or occupancy consent)
Capital contribution receipts or bank transfer confirmations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ later queries the description of management authority or contributions, file a notarial affidavit of the general partner together with payment receipts and the relevant partnership agreement articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online declaration and payment portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Connect to the REQ online service using a secured account. Complete the Déclaration d'immatriculation with the partnership's legal name, registered office, establishments, general partner, manager and principal activities, which should reference ISIC 3240 / NAICS 315280 (costume and theatrical apparel manufacturing). Pay the applicable filing duty by credit card or Interac. Retain the electronic acknowledgement until the attestation is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ online declaration form
Certified copy of the signed partnership agreement
Government-issued identification of the general partner and manager
Registered office and establishment address particulars
Description of planned activities under ISIC 3240 / NAICS 315280
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues an incompleteness notice under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, cure the file within 30 days by filing supplementary declarations. If the deadline is missed, a new declaration and a fresh filing duty are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – public registry and attestation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, review the REQ attestation verifying the partnership's legal name, enterprise number (NEQ), entity type, date of registration, registered office, establishments and signatory managers. Order certified copies of the attestation for banking and counterparty use. If any ultimate beneficial owner information is required under applicable law, file the necessary declaration online through REQ.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation certificate
Public extract of the registered enterprise
Change declaration if any registered information has changed
Beneficial ownership declaration record when applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the attestation contains an inaccuracy, file a declaration of modification with REQ supported by the partnership agreement and a resolution of the general partner to correct the public record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Payroll and Banking Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec, Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), commercial banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the REQ one-stop government service to transmit the registered information to Revenu Québec and obtain the tax accounts (QST, GST/HST, and source deductions). Confirm with CRA or Revenu Québec the Business Number and provincial account numbers. Open a Canadian commercial bank account in the partnership's name, requesting bank KYC forms and a corporate resolution proving authorized signatories.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation certificate
Certified partnership agreement
Form RC159 for CRA and Revenu Québec LM-1 application where applicable
Resolution of the general partner confirming authorized signatories
Proof of registered office and bank account request forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec queries the tax registration, resubmit the REQ attestation, partnership agreement, and a certified resolution of general partners clarifying management authority and valid banking signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Workplace and Environmental Compliance Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality, Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ), CNESST, and Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal occupancy permit for the manufacturing unit. Where building changes are planned, engage a licensed engineer to confirm structural load capacity and file for RBQ approval as needed. Register with CNESST for workplace health and safety, establish a prevention program, and elect a health and safety representative if required. If industrial activity may release contaminants, file relevant environmental declarations or ministerial authorization requests with MELCCFP before operations begin.
required_dossiers: Municipal occupancy permit application
RBQ construction/alteration permit if applicable
Structural load report signed by a licensed engineer
CNESST employer registration confirmation and prevention program
MELCCFP declaration or authorization application for air/wastewater
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any permit refusal is cured by addressing the technical objections, revising the plans with a qualified engineer, and providing additional risk-control measures to the municipality, CNESST or MELCCFP. A final refusal may be challenged before the Tribunal administratif du Québec where authorized by law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipalité locale (bureau des permis), Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ), CNESST, and MELCCFP
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal occupancy permit (permis d'occupation) and, where applicable, ministerial authorization or declaration under the Environment Quality Act; no separate Quebec provincial manufacturing license is imposed for ISIC 3240 / NAICS 315280 costume apparel manufacturing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration/ministerial authorization route: a full EIA is not mandatory for a standard cut-and-sew costume and wig manufacturing operation unless Schedule III of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (REAE) is triggered by specific contaminant discharges; a declaration or ministerial authorization is required where emissions or sewer discharge are present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer must respect municipal sewer by-laws and MELCCFP approval conditions: pH 6.0-9.5; BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L; suspended solids not exceeding 350 mg/L; oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L. Air emissions from solvent-based adhesives and finishing products must not exceed the company-specific ministerial authorization threshold, typically 0.5 kg/h of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) per emission point unless a lower local limit is imposed; no CFC-based products are permitted. Solid waste including expired adhesives and dyes must be characterized and, if hazardous, manifested under the Regulation respecting the recovery and disposal of residual materials.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire prevention service confirming fire extinguishers, emergency exits, alarms, emergency lighting and fire separation; structural load inspection report by a licensed engineer covering storage racks and industrial equipment; CNESST occupational safety registration, prevention program, first-aid kit and workplace signage; RBQ electrical conformity certificate for industrial wiring and equipment installation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal competent authority for the Business Number (BN) and GST/HST — accessed via the CRA My Business Account portal (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses.html). Because the LP has a Quebec establishment, the federal-provincial Single Tax Administration Agreement designates Revenu Québec as the sole administrator of both GST/HST and the provincial Quebec Sales Tax (QST); Revenu Québec operates the Clic Revenu / ARGENT digital portal (revenuquebec.ca). The Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) remains the upstream mandatory business registry for the juridical existence of the limited partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Complete REQ registration of the LP to obtain the Quebec establishment number (NEQ). 2) Apply for tax accounts through the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or the Revenu Québec entrepreneur platform; authorize a representative with a valid mandate. 3) CRA issues the 9-digit Business Number (BN); the GST/HST program account (RT prefix) opens concurrently and Revenu Québec assigns the QST registration number (RQ file number) in a single data exchange. 4) The LP registers in its own name as a 'person' for GST/QST purposes even though it is fiscally transparent for income tax. 5) Registration is mandatory on the day total taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or cumulatively in the four preceding quarters; voluntary registration may be requested earlier. 6) On failure to register, CRA may register the LP retroactively under ETA s. 240(2) and assess penalties from the date registration was required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for income tax: income, losses, capital gains, and credits are computed at the partnership level and allocated to partners per the partnership agreement (ITA s. 96; Quebec Taxation Act). The LP files only an information return (T5013 federal and the Quebec partnership information return) and pays no entity-level income tax. By contrast, for GST/HST and QST the LP is a separate registrant and is itself the taxable supplier; partners are jointly and severally liable for the partnership's net tax obligations. Territorial scope: resident partners are worldwide-taxed; non-resident partners are subject to Canadian and Quebec tax on their allocable share of the LP's Canadian-source business income and are deemed to have a permanent establishment in Canada via the partnership (ITA s. 253.1).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists for a Canadian LP; the entity cannot elect to be taxed as a corporation. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1 (Form T1139) permitting a non-calendar partnership year-end when all partners' taxation years coincide; (ii) closely related election under ETA s. 156(2) to alter the deemed-nil-consideration rule and make taxable supplies between the partnership and related entities; (iii) no prophylactic hybrid mismatch election is granted — Canada applies BEPS Action 2 rules that re-characterize certain foreign check-the-box entities and hybrid financial instrument deductions, and any structuring involving non-resident limited partners must be validated against those anti-avoidance provisions before reliance on pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax, 5%) layered with the Quebec Sales Tax (QST, 9.5%). Quebec is not an HST participating province; the QST is legally computed on the GST-inclusive selling price, producing an effective combined indirect burden of 14.975% of the pre-tax invoice price. GST/HST is governed by the Excise Tax Act; QST is governed by the Quebec Taxation Act and administered by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable worldwide supplies made in a single calendar quarter or cumulatively over the four preceding calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold; ETA s. 148; the QST threshold is identical by administrative agreement). Upon crossing the single-quarter threshold, registration is compulsory effective that same day; upon crossing the four-quarter test, registration is effective at the beginning of the first month after the threshold is exceeded. The LP may also register voluntarily as soon as it makes any taxable supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government API-based invoice stamping, no digital seal, and no mandatory B2B e-invoicing platform as of 2025; Quebec's planned mandatory electronic invoicing reform remains indefinitely suspended. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices that contain all prescribed invoice content. However, for exported goods, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) requires electronic filing of the export declaration (B13A) through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for shipments valued above CAD 2,000 or subject to permits/controls, generating an export confirmation reference that must be preserved for tax audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods — cosplay costumes, licensed theatrical prop apparel, and synthetic wigs — may be zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, para. 1 when: the supplier and the non-resident recipient deal at arm's length; the goods are delivered in Canada to the non-resident recipient; the goods will not be further processed or incorporated into goods supplied in Canada; and the goods leave Canada as soon as is reasonably possible after delivery (CRA administrative benchmark: generally within 60 days). Direct-to-consumer international shipments by mail or courier to a foreign address likewise qualify. Offshore services supplied to a non-resident (e.g., design or web-store services) qualify under Part V, para. 7 only where they do not relate to real property or tangible property situated in Canada. The QST zero-rating rules for Quebec mirror the GST rules; Canada imposes no exchange-control or FX-repatriation requirement, so the operative deadline is the 60-day export window.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or CBSA CERS electronic export-reporting confirmation with export reference number
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / Ocean Waybill evidencing shipment of the costumes or wigs to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice and purchase order naming the non-resident buyer and destination country
Inward remittance or bank settlement certificate evidencing payment in convertible currency from the non-resident buyer
Freight-forwarder certificate, insurance policy, or courier tracking report evidencing exit from Canada, together with the destination customs entry if available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess GST/QST within four years, extended to ten years where a return was filed with misrepresentation, carelessness, or fraud (ETA s. 298 and Quebec parallel rules). Zero-rating claimed without substantiation is reassessed at the full 14.975% effective combined rate, plus daily-compounded prescribed interest from the original filing date. Civil penalties include 5%-10% of unremitted tax plus fixed penalties for failure to register, file, or remit (ETA s. 280), and a substantial false-statement penalty of up to 25% of the amount at issue for negligent claims (ETA s. 285). Fraudulent export zero-rating or forgery of export documents is a criminal offence under ETA s. 327, punishable by fines of up to 100% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment. CRA operates an Export Verification Program that targets high-risk exporters; records supporting zero-rating must be retained for six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the prudential regulator for federally licensed banks; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/ATF financial intelligence unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility for the Canadian dollar (CAD). The currency is freely floating with no exchange controls or surrender requirements. Capital contributions and profit remittances are not subject to central bank approval; however, payments of certain income streams to non-resident partners may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (base statutory 25%, generally reduced by an applicable tax treaty).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in a foreign currency, converted at market rates, or credited to a Canadian-dollar account. All international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC by the financial intermediary under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary settlement rail, not a substitute for a Schedule I bank relationship. Legal constraints: foreign digital EMI platforms (e.g., Payoneer, Wise Business) are not Canadian banks, are not CDIC-insured, and cannot clear CAD directly through Payments Canada. They may be used for e-commerce payout aggregation and cross-border supplier payments, but the core capital escrow, FX, and LC infrastructure must sit with an OSFI-regulated or provincially regulated (Quebec) deposit-taking institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person attendance is mandatory for the general partner or a duly authorized signatory at a Canadian branch of the chosen bank. Remote account opening is not generally available for newly formed non-resident-controlled limited partnerships. The authorized individual must produce original identification, the LP registration certificate from the Quebec Registraire des entreprises, partnership agreement, good standing proof, and a source-of-funds declaration. Some banks will allow a videoconference only as a supplement to a notarized or apostilled identity verification performed in the director's home country, but the branch interview is normally a hard mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners and absence of a Canadian-resident ultimate beneficial owner with banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership declaration (Déclaration immatriculation), notarized partnership agreement, register of beneficial owners under Quebec’s Business Registration Act, proof of identity and residential address for all partners, a formal delegation of authority to a Canadian general partner, and a legal opinion confirming the LP’s existence and borrowing capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive e-commerce revenue through Stripe and Shopify Payments with high chargeback expectations for custom cosplay apparel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant processing statements, refund and return policy, chargeback dispute management logs, order-level CRM records, shipping and delivery confirmations, inventory purchase invoices from licensed wig and fabric suppliers, and bank-deposit reconciliation reports tracing the settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border supplier payments to jurisdictions with known money-laundering or sanctions vulnerabilities (e.g., synthetic wig/traditional theatrical textile hubs in Asia).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma invoices and purchase orders, bills of lading and airway bills, customs entry documentation, HS tariff classification certificates, completed know-your-supplier questionnaires, sanctions-screening results, and a written trade rationale linked to ISIC 3240/NAICS 315280 operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership has no statutory minimum capital, raising questions about genuine commercial substance and ability to settle trade obligations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and projected cash flow model, signed lease or sublease for a physical manufacturing/warehouse premise in Quebec, local payroll and independent contractor agreements, CRA and Revenu Québec registration entries, T5013 partnership information return filings, and evidence of trade credit or existing customer contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident partners must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from their home bank to the LP’s CDIC-insured Canadian operating or escrow account. For transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, the receiving Canadian bank is required to file an international electronic funds transfer report with FINTRAC. The payment reference must include the LP’s Quebec enterprise registration number and the explicit purpose 'Capital contribution to Canadian limited partnership'. Prior to first receipt, the bank will verify the source of funds; accept only authenticated corporate bank accounts in the partner’s own name to avoid AML rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements use two standard clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire payments of royalties, subcontractor invoices, and low-value raw materials; and (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700, UCP600) for large or recurring purchases where shipment documents are required. CAD domestic settlements clear through Payments Canada’s Large Value Transfer System (LVTS), while USD and cross-border payments transit through correspondent banks and the SWIFT network. All outbound remittances are screened against OFAC, UN, EU, and Canadian sanctions lists; include the underlying purchase order and commercial invoice numbers in the payment narrative.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP foreign exchange swaps
Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars
Cross-currency interest rate swaps where the LP has committed debt facilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for supplier currencies that lack a fully convertible onshore forward market, subject to the Canadian bank’s internal credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the partnership registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CAD 100 penalty; continued default beyond 12 months may result in administrative strike-off from the registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutorily compulsory independent audit for a non-reporting limited partnership; an audit or review may become mandatory if required by the partnership agreement, at partner request, or for projects exceeding CAD 2M gross annual revenue under contractual covenants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (for reporting/foreign serves) or Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for domestic non-public entities; U.S. GAAP accepted for US-member pass-through reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual declaration must confirm all general partners and disclose any transfer of limited partnership units exceeding 10% of contributed capital; updated register entries and UBO details are due within 30 days of any transfer, and these must be current as of the anniversary declaration date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of the Corporate General Partner (if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,000 (if voluntarily contracted; no statutory audit required)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%) general corporate active business rate; the Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent, so this rate applies at the corporate-partner level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A qualifying CCPC corporate partner may claim the Small Business Deduction (9% federal on first CAD 500,000) and Quebec's reduced SME rate (3.2%) for a combined 12.2% effective rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income. Manufacturing assets used in cosplay costume/prop apparel fabrication may qualify for accelerated CCA (Class 29/50) and Quebec manufacturing-investment tax credits. Federal and Quebec non-capital losses may generally be carried back 3 years and carried forward 20 years.
